may: locate, copy, hash, classify, and admit donor artifacts
record rights, claim boundaries, failure states, and missing evidence
reject a donor whose identity, provenance, integrity, or recovery path cannot be reproduced
may_not: promote a donor into the successor interface
treat a located artifact as durably archived
close JDB99-001 while any required custody gap remains open
alter the historical public Manzanita route during custody work
invent missing canonical task rows or convert remembered counts into recovered records

qualification_boundary: A passing custody validation proves only that the current register, repository-resident hashes, historical-route guard, donor anchors, and declared gaps agree on one exact head. It does not close JDB99-001, qualify a public Manzanita release, perform an external campaign, repair the lost canonical backlog, or transfer product authority.

hash_law.manifest_encoding: UTF-8 canonical JSON with sorted keys

public_route_guard.failure_message: Any mismatch means custody work changed or failed to recover the historical public route. Stop integration and investigate before merging.

donors.claim_boundary: Historical public rollback donor. Its retained qualification applies only to the tests and public surface it actually carried; it is not the successor or proof of the current internal chain.

donors.location: repository, Git history, and retained source-foundation receipt
donors.claim_boundary: Governed live-data and Street Glide source foundation. It is a donor data plane, not a released interface or complete provider-operations campaign.
Contained internal multidisciplinary review machinery. It is not external endorsement or independent public-release authority.
Internal design constitution and specimen. It does not establish whole-product finish, field fitness, or public release.
One source-backed public-safe demonstration place. It is not a private household, field finding, or public successor endpoint.
Seven internal operational apertures. They do not grant private, field, or adverse-action standing.
Provider-order scene resolver and image-edge registration kernel. A registered image edge is not a surveyed or physically interpreted feature.
Eight registered internal overlay instruments. Authored geometry and unavailable sources remain non-observational.
Five functional projections and a bounded internal FAB handoff. Visibility and preparation do not become consent, eligibility, execution, or external effect.
Complete internal operating composition. It is not the exact public endpoint or proof of physical and human campaigns.
Automated resilience and browser qualification floor. Chromium campaigns do not substitute for real assistive technology, people, hardware, networks, or deployed bytes.
Complete source-surface disposition accounting. Accounting does not qualify, absorb, supersede, or close the underlying estate products.

Byte-addressed internal release candidate, local served-byte proof, isolated same-runner verification, and local rollback mechanism. Public endpoint, real rollback, and independently operated succession remain separate campaigns.
Local-first evidence instrument for ten external campaigns. The runner, its tests, and a complete form do not prove that any real campaign occurred or authorize release.
Program law, recovery evidence, and governance controls. The original row-level 497-task machine register remains unavailable and remembered counts are not task-row evidence.
Repository Pages deployment receipt. It does not prove that the internal successor replaced the historical /manzanita/ route or that the exact successor bytes passed a public-endpoint campaign.
Acquisition and receipt machinery plus retained source states. It does not establish complete provider credentials, quotas, terms, costs, outages, or every required degradation campaign.

gaps.target: Enumerate and retain every Manzanita release, rejected candidate, failed build, and externally circulated package before and after 1.4.0.
gaps.admission: Each object has an immutable commit or package identity, complete file manifest, SHA-256 hashes, disposition, and claim boundary.
gaps.failure_mode: A predecessor or rejected build disappears behind the labels old, superseded, or failed.

gaps.target: Locate and retain every approved and rejected full-state visual golden across desktop, laptop, tablet, mobile, compact, light, dark, reduced-motion, failure, and degraded states.
gaps.admission: Each image is tied to route, commit, viewport, theme, state, browser, capture method, and acceptance or rejection disposition.
gaps.failure_mode: A later build imitates a selected crop while losing the complete state that was reviewed.

gaps.target: Recover and retain representative-seat playtests, assistive-technology observations, device and network campaigns, field sessions, and cold-successor transcripts.
gaps.admission: Every finding names the actor, venue, procedure, exact build, observation, evidence, severity, acceptance, and disposition.
gaps.failure_mode: Automation or a summary is later presented as the human or physical campaign it was designed to support.

gaps.target: Retain failed CI runs, deployment failures, rejected-release receipts, provider failures, source contradictions, no-coverage states, and the design rules derived from them.
gaps.admission: Each failure has a stable run or file identity, bounded logs, affected commit, classification, and resulting rule or disposition.
gaps.failure_mode: A successful rerun erases the causal evidence for the correction that followed.

gaps.target: Retain the complete admitted live-data corpus across successful, empty, stale, contradictory, missing-credential, rate-limited, outage, terms-blocked, cost-blocked, and revocation states.
gaps.admission: Every payload and receipt preserves request, response class, source time, retrieval time, transform, attribution, rights, cache rule, uncertainty, and degradation state.
gaps.failure_mode: Only happy-path source data remains available for later qualification.

gaps.target: Backfill Manzanita-specific deployment receipts and exact observed public-byte manifests for every prior release, failed deployment, and rollback.
gaps.admission: Every deployed or attempted release has source commit, artifact digest, endpoint, run identity, observed public manifest, outcome, and rollback target.
gaps.failure_mode: Repository state or a generic Pages receipt is mistaken for the bytes that reached the Manzanita endpoint.

gaps.target: Locate original sourced, captured, authored, modeled, generated, and transformed visual assets with rights and claim receipts.
gaps.admission: Each asset has original bytes or stable source, creator or provider, acquisition date, rights class, transforms, generated-state label where applicable, and permitted claims.
gaps.failure_mode: A polished image becomes an unattributed orphan or is later mistaken for observed evidence.

gaps.target: Locate standalone Manzanita HTML, ZIP, PDF, image, print, handoff, and operator-pack exports that existed outside the current repository tree.
gaps.admission: Each export has complete bytes, SHA-256, production date, source build, purpose, recipient class, and supersession status.
gaps.failure_mode: An externally circulated artifact cannot be reproduced or distinguished from the canonical route.

gaps.target: Mirror every qualification artifact from the source foundation through P10 and the campaign runner into independently controlled durable storage with readback receipts.
gaps.admission: Each mirror retains exact bytes and authoritative SHA-256, a documented recovery path, permissions metadata, and a cold-successor replay receipt.
gaps.failure_mode: Qualification depends on expiring Actions storage, one account, or a narrative digest without recoverable bytes.

gaps.target: Recover the original complete row-level Manzanita 497-task register or admit a separately identified successor register with per-row provenance.
gaps.admission: One governed source contains complete unique rows, required fields, dependencies, amendments, family and priority counts, stable JSON and CSV digests, and an explicit distinction between recovered and newly authored records.
gaps.failure_mode: Remembered counts or later PRs are converted into fabricated canonical task closures.

gaps.target: Execute and retain the real external campaigns required by release control, including public-endpoint and deployed-rollback evidence, without allowing the runner itself to count as the campaign.
gaps.admission: Each campaign carries an accountable operator, actual venue, versioned procedure, complete observations, exact evidence, acceptance, failure disposition, and separate release-authority review.
gaps.failure_mode: A complete form, passing test, or initialized workspace is treated as physical, human, deployed, or public standing.
